title: feat(BUG-0019 W2): flag-off connection pool for openai-compatible SSE
body:
## Summary

Implements **Wave W2** of PLAN-v1.00.15 (BUG-0019): connection pooling for openai-compatible SSE streams, **flag-gated, DEFAULT OFF** (`networking.pool.enabled=false` → byte-for-byte legacy behavior).

### New module `llm/conn-pool.rkt`
- Host-keyed pool on `(host, port, tls?)`; per-entry custodians parented by the pool custodian (never request-scoped)
- Idle TTL 55s (< typical server keep-alive); `max-per-host` 4 enforced at check-in
- Single-use-on-fault: any fault discards, never re-handed-out
- Deterministic-framing reuse rule: only Content-Length responses check in; chunked/EOF-delimited bodies stay single-use (deliberate W2 limitation — SSE is usually chunked)
- Fresh boxes minted at check-in (a shared-box bug the fd-leak probe caught: pooled entries inherited `released?#t`, making subsequent releases silent no-ops)
- Stats (hits/misses/evictions/fault-closes) for W3 bake evidence

### Pool-aware teardown in `openai-compatible.rkt`
Pooled requests skip the request-scoped custodian entirely (the BUG_PLAN landmine: its shutdown would kill pooled sockets); cleanup releases the entry instead. Flag-off path unchanged.

### Wiring
`networking.pool.{enabled,idle-ttl-secs,max-per-host}` wired via new `wire-connection-pool!` in both CLI run-mode startup and loop config reload.

### Tests (`tests/test-conn-pool.rkt`, 8 passing)
Roundtrip reuse (miss→hit), TTL eviction, max-per-host cap, single-use-on-fault, wiring matrix (absent/false/true), and a 100-cycle fd-leak stress test asserting fds return to baseline after shutdown.

title: fix(BUG-0019 W0+W1): FIN/CLOSE-WAIT-aware SSE liveness watchdog
body:
## Summary

Implements waves W0+W1 of [PLAN-v1.00.15](https://github.com/coinerd/q/blob/main/.planning-mirror) (BUG-0019: SSE stream hangs up to the full phase timeout when the peer closes without TLS close_notify).

**W0** — deterministic reproducer:
- `tests/reproducers/mock-fin-server.rkt`: local TLS server with 4 modes (`unclean-close`, `clean-close`, `heartbeat-alive`, `true-silence`), self-signed cert at setup
- `tests/reproducers/probe-fin-detection.rkt`: Step-C experiment; recorded platform verdict

**W1** — FIN-aware liveness watchdog in `stream-sse-events`:
- Byte-level pump slices idle windows into `peer-close-probe-secs` (default 5s) slices; zero-timeout probe read at each boundary
- Unclean peer close → new `exn:fail:network:peer-closed` (fields: `phase`, `data-received?`, `content-chars`, `elapsed-ms`; SS-5-style message suffix) raised **in <1s regardless of thinking-gap-cap**
- EOF stays normal end-of-stream; heartbeat/data bytes reset the probe clock (BUG-0018 liveness rule preserved)
- `request-policy.rkt`: additive `current-peer-close-probe-secs` parameter + inventory entries
- `auto-retry.rkt`: peer-closed classified timeout-tier; v1.00.14 silent-overflow economics unchanged

## Platform finding (recorded in STATE)

On Racket 8.10/OpenSSL 3.x an unclean FIN raises `exn:fail:network` (never plain EOF), so ladder option 1 (non-blocking probe + error capture) suffices — FFI getsockopt not needed. True TLS close_notify EOF is unobservable even from graceful server closes; clean end-of-stream relies on the SSE `[DONE]` marker (as real providers signal it).

## Test plan

- [x] `tests/test-stream-peer-close.rkt` 10/10 (FIN ≤5s w/ cap 900; DONE-based clean end; heartbeat never killed; true-silence timeout intact; retry classification)
- [x] Regression guards unchanged: midstream-stall, sse-phase-timeout-bounds, request-network-policy, auto-retry, stream (220 tests)
- [x] Fast suite: 1116 pass; only pre-existing/environmental failures remain (documented in STATE-v1.00.15)
- [x] raco fmt + raco make clean on all changed files

title: fix(gsd): tolerate em-dash wave headers + 1-based plan numbering (v1.00.14 hotfix)
body:
## v1.00.14 hotfix — /go plan normalization rejected em-dash wave headers

**Observed (session MN5MQHQP):**
```
Plan normalization failed: Wave indices not sequential 0..3: (0 0 0 0)
```

**Root cause:** `parse-wave-section-raw` only matched `## Wave N: Title` (colon
separator). The user's plan used `## Wave 1 — Title` (em-dash), so the header
regex failed silently and every wave fell back to index 0 → `(0 0 0 0)`.
Secondary: the plan was written with human 1-based numbering (Wave 1..4),
while internal indexing is 0-based.

### Fix
- **plan-types-parser.rkt**: header separator may be `:`, em/en-dash (`—`/`–`),
  or a hyphen run (`-`)
- **plan-types.rkt** `parse-waves-from-markdown`: an EXACT 1..n sequential run
  is normalized to 0-based; anything else left untouched so normalize-plan
  still rejects genuinely broken numbering (e.g. `(2 5)` stays `(2 5)`)

### Test
`tests/test-plan-wave-header-tolerance.rkt` reproduces the exact failing plan
shape (em-dash + DONE markers + Wave 1..4) and asserts normalization now
succeeds. Classic colon plans unchanged. Existing GSD plan tests green
(171 passed). Format lint PASSED.

title: fix(BUG-0018): thinking-gap cap, /model request-path fix, retry economics (v1.00.14)

## BUG-0018 remediation — v1.00.14

Closes BUG-0018 (.planning/bugs/BUG-0018-glm-thinking-timeout-model-switch-ineffective): GLM-5.3 silent-thinking >300s timeout/retry loop and ineffective /model switch.

### W1 — Configurable thinking-gap ceiling + keepalive liveness
- New per-model config key `timeouts.models.<model>.thinking-gap-cap` widens the SSE thinking-idle window past the legacy 300s bound (**widen-only** precedence)
- Ops-level parameter `current-max-thinking-gap-secs` (default 300) — default behavior identical to v1.00.13
- Keepalive liveness: heartbeat frames / zero-delta chunks reset the idle clock; only true silence or total budget raises (`test-midstream-stall.rkt`)

- **R-B1 root cause**: `build-session-context-for-prompt` E4 re-applied the path-derived model name on *every* prompt, silently reverting `/model` switches
- `set-model!`/`switch-model!` now record an explicit `'model-override` marker; E4 defers to it

- **R-B2**: `handle-model-command` refuses UI-only switches when no live session exists; guarantees `model.switched` publish (logger fallback when bus nil); transcript entry only after mutation success

### W3 — Retry economics + executor inheritance
- Silent-thinking overflows (thinking phase, zero visible chars) get exactly ONE retry, then circuit-break with guidance ("raise thinking-gap-cap or /model switch"); backoff scales with consumed window
- GSD `/go` executor sessions inherit the coordinator's switched provider/model (`runtime/session/executor-inheritance.rkt`, R-B3)

### Testing
159 tests across `test-request-network-policy`, `test-sse-phase-timeout-bounds`, `test-midstream-stall`, `test-auto-retry`, `test-model-command`, `test-executor-inheritance`, `test-provider-recovery-model-switch-e2e` — all green. Format lint PASSED.

title: fix(gsd): S2a — truncate lease lock before rewrite + sanitize empty owner (#9358)
body:
Closes #9358 (part of parent #9355).

**Problem:** Campaign 81f9be4b attempt-5 lock corruption: `open-output-file 'can-update` does NOT truncate, so `file-position 0` + write left a stale tail from the previous (longer) owner — observed: `#hasheq((acquired . ...) (owner . "") (pid . 1194981))VGGEKK0") (pid . 1194981))`. The lease file became unreadable, defeating D4 owner diagnostics. The re-dispatch path also wrote `(owner . "")`, so a stale lease could not be attributed.

**Fix:**
- `file-truncate port 0` before rewriting the lease.
- Sanitize owner: empty/missing session-id falls back to `"unknown"`.
- `campaign-lease` records the sanitized owner.

**Tests:** `tests/test-gsd-go-orchestrator.rkt` +2 — stale-tail truncation regression (previous longer owner must not leave fragments) and empty-owner sanitization.

## Fix: workspace bytecode wipe deletes the tracked discovery fixture

### Root cause (named by the #9496 diagnostic)

The third v1.00.13 tag-publish run failed the release git-clean gate with:

```
[FAIL] git has 1 uncommitted change(s)
  D tests/metadata-discovery/fixture/tests/compiled/stray-test.rkt

```
find . -type f -name '*.zo' -delete
find . -depth -type d -name compiled -exec rm -rf {} +

Exclude `./tests/metadata-discovery/fixture/*` from all three wipes (the fixture contains no bytecode by design). `prepare-racket-environment` only *copies* compiled dirs — untouched.

- Exclusion verified locally: `find ... -not -path './tests/metadata-discovery/fixture/*'` no longer matches the fixture dir; unfiltered find still does

title: feat(liveness): v1.00.13 W4 — connect/TTFB bound, hard deadlines, heartbeat-aware liveness (#9478)
body:
W4 of v1.00.13 (#886) — liveness + deadline completion (RL-4/RL-8/RL-9, NP-7). **Broad-gate wave.**

## What
- **Connect/TTFB bound (RL-4)** — `provider-sendrecv/ttfb-bounded` (http-helpers): connect+TLS+status+headers runs under the policy window `min(request, 120)`; an established-but-silent peer raises `exn:fail:network:timeout:stream` with structured phase `'connect/ttfb` — never the full request budget (previously up to 900 s). Cleanup runs before the worker is killed. All four adapters wire it on streaming paths and pass `#:connect-timeout` on eager paths.
- **Hard remaining-budget reads (NP-7)** — every blocking stream read waits at most `min(phase-idle, remaining-total)`: a read can no longer overshoot the total wall-clock deadline by a full phase window.
- **Heartbeat-aware held-request classification (RL-8)** — `held-request?` consults heartbeat metadata: a heartbeat-only stream is live-but-no-content (retryable), only zero-liveness silent 200s trip the breaker; total deadline + flood ceiling still bound heartbeat-only streams.
- **Tests** — `test-stream-liveness-classification.rkt` promoted green and extended into the W4 matrix: silent-peer connect/TTFB bound with elapsed assertion, total-deadline overshoot prevention, cancellation responsiveness (break, never timeout).
- Migration-proof suite added early (`test-request-policy-migration.rkt`: DeepSeek `request:900 sse-read:600` and Kimi `sse-read:300` shapes, explicit-keys-win, caps hold).

## Evidence
18 focused suites green; **security suite 64/64**; arch suite green after registering the `llm/http-helpers.rkt` hotspot risk-note (module grew into the lifecycle executor per plan W3 task 1). Broad gate: 1299/1301 — `test-tmux-explore-campaign` requires the repo SHA to exist on GitHub (attestation), so it validates on this pushed branch rather than on the local pre-push tree (verified: passes on pushed SHAs); `test-arch-fitness` fixed by the risk-note.

title: feat(lifecycle): v1.00.13 W3 — headers, cleanup, structured failures (#9473)
body:
W3 of v1.00.13 (#886) — request lifecycle ownership: headers, cleanup, structured failures (RL-5/RL-6/RL-7).

## What
- **Structured failure context** (`llm/http-helpers.rkt`): `build-network-failure-context` (kind / http-status / redacted response-headers / parsed retry-after-ms). Response headers are REDACTED to the retry-relevant subset (`Retry-After`, `x-ratelimit-*`) — authorization/cookie values never reach failure metadata or logs.
- **`parse-retry-after-header`**: delta-seconds AND HTTP-date forms. The date parser is timezone-free (civil-calendar conversion — `find-seconds` is locale-dependent) with a deterministic `#:now-ms` clock seam; past dates clamp to 0.
- **Deterministic port ownership** (RL-6): `make-provider-http-request` closes every response port exactly once — success, status-check failure, read timeout, request timeout (cleanup passed to the request-timeout wrapper), cancellation (dynamic-wind post-thunk). Provider errors from status checkers are re-raised with the structured context attached.
- **`current-provider-http-sendrecv`**: injectable HTTP boundary for the cleanup-contract tests.
- **Retry consumes structure, not strings** (RL-7): `structured-retry-after-ms` (auto-retry) reads the context hash only; `with-auto-retry` no longer feeds the exception message to `parse-retry-after`. `provider-error-context` accessor exported from provider-errors.
- Duration contracts widened `exact-positive-integer?` → `positive?` (matches downstream wrappers; enables sub-second test durations).

title: fix(llm): wire per-model sse-read config into SSE stream timeouts (wave-cancelled SSE stalls)
body:
## Summary

Fixes the repeated `wave-cancelled` SSE-read timeouts on the default provider (glm-5.3). Root cause: the `timeouts.models.<model>.sse-read` config key was **dead** — `wire-timeouts!` only read `request`, and the SSE stream timeouts came from hardcoded constants:
- thinking/initial cap `held-request-detect-secs = 120` (openai-compatible.rkt)
- content per-chunk `http-stream-timeout-default = 60` (stream.rkt)

glm-5.3 had no config entry, so it fell back to the 120s cap → repeated `HTTP read timeout (120 seconds) waiting for SSE chunk` → wave-cancelled. (A second variant, `HTTP read timeout (60 seconds)`, hit the content-phase constant during W6.)

## Changes

- **`llm/stream.rkt`**: new `current-model-sse-read-timeouts` parameter + `effective-sse-read-timeout-for` (returns `#f` when no per-model override)
- **`wiring/mode-helpers.rkt`**: `wire-timeouts!` populates the new parameter from `timeouts.models.<model>.sse-read`
- **`llm/openai-compatible.rkt`**: `openai-stream-request` threads the model's sse-read timeout through; thinking/initial cap and content-phase per-chunk timeout use it, falling back to the v0.99.78 defaults (120/60) when no override
- **`tests/test-model-timeouts.rkt`**: +8 tests (effective-sse-read-timeout-for semantics + wiring extraction)

## Config

`~/.q/config.json` now has `timeouts.models.glm-5.3 = {request: 900, sse-read: 300}` (applied).

## Effect

| Model | Before | After |
|-------|--------|-------|
| glm-5.3 | thinking 120s / content 60s | **300s / 300s** |
| deepseek-v4-flash | thinking 120s / content 60s | 60s / 60s (per its config, unchanged) |
| models w/o override | 120s / 60s | 120s / 60s (unchanged) |

Verified end-to-end: `wire-timeouts!` on the real config → `effective-sse-read-timeout-for "glm-5.3"` = 300, `"deepseek-v4-flash"` = 60, unknown = `#f` → defaults. Lint: 24/24 pass. Fast suite: 1101/1103 (2 known pre-existing flakes).

title: fix(security): recanonicalize LF3 link targets

## Root cause

On macOS, a symlink may resolve to an absolute path that still contains a lexical alias such as `/var`, while the configured allowed root is already canonical (`/private/var`). The prior resolver advanced from the resolved target without walking its alias-bearing components again, causing valid in-root paths to be rejected.

## Fix

When an existing component resolves to a different target, restart longest-prefix traversal from that target and append the original remaining tail. This canonicalizes alias-bearing absolute targets before the fail-closed root containment comparison.

## Regression coverage

Adds a portable fixture whose absolute link target passes through a lexical allowed-root alias. It fails on the prior resolver and passes with this repair; all 36 worker-security tests pass.

title: fix(gsd): delivery verifier recognizes merged-to-main wave delivery
body:
## Fix: delivery verifier recognizes merged-to-main wave delivery

### Problem
When a wave agent executes waves step by step and its work is committed + **merged to main** (the v1.00.06 flow), the local `HEAD` equals `origin/main` after the merge, so `git diff origin/main...HEAD` is empty. The verifier then reports:

```
files: no wave target files changed: .github/workflows/full-regression.yml, scripts/run-tests/reporting.rkt
```

even though the target files **were** changed during the campaign. This is the same false-negative family as:
- #9382 (committed-branch delivery recognized)
- #9386 (annotations + retry-with-adaptation)
- #9390 (directory wave targets)
- #9399 (git-root-relative wave file paths)

### Fix
Thread the campaign's `created-at` epoch through:
`make-delivery-verifier` → `run-delivery-verification` → `check-wave-files-changed` → `changed-files-set`.

When `created-at` is known, `changed-files-set` also collects files changed in commits reachable from `HEAD` since the **campaign base commit** (`git rev-list -1 --before=<epoch> HEAD` → `git diff <base> HEAD`). Merged-to-main delivery is thereby recognized as valid evidence, without weakening the per-wave gate: the wave target files must still appear in the changed set.

`command-handlers.rkt` passes `(campaign-record-created-at rec)` when constructing the verifier.

### Test
Added a regression test: a campaign whose wave work is committed + merged to main is **rejected** without `created-at` (old behavior) and **approved** with `created-at`. All 16 delivery-verifier tests pass.

### Verify
- `racket tests/test-gsd-delivery-verifier.rkt` → 16/16 pass
- `racket tests/test-gsd-go-orchestrator.rkt`, `test-gsd-wave-completion.rkt`, `test-gsd-command-handlers-unit.rkt`, `test-gsd-campaign-state.rkt` → pass

## v1.00.05 Wave 2 (#9394): Interactive/planning retry = 5 + ceiling reconciliation

### Problem
The `/plan` gsd-planning session on `kimi-for-coding` showed `[retry: LLM timeout, 1/2...]` — only 2 retries, not the 5 used by campaign waves. Two latent bugs compounded:
1. `current-provider-retry-max-retries` default was **2**; only campaign execution (`execute-campaign-request!`) parameterized it to 5. Interactive turns used the 2 default.
2. Even with max-retries=5, `call-with-provider-retry` did **not** pass `#:per-type-budgets`, so `with-auto-retry`'s default `'timeout` budget of **2** silently capped timeout retries at 2 — **both** interactive and campaign paths.
3. `default-cumulative-ceiling-secs` = 300s truncated the loop after ~2 attempts at 120s-per-read.

### Changes
- **`runtime/provider-retry.rkt`**: default `current-provider-retry-max-retries` 2 → **5** (interactive/planning now matches campaign).
- **`runtime/provider-retry.rkt`**: `call-with-provider-retry` now passes `#:per-type-budgets` derived from max-retries (`'timeout n 'rate-limit (max 4 n) 'provider-error n`), so the timeout budget no longer caps retries below max-retries.
- **`runtime/auto-retry.rkt`**: `default-cumulative-ceiling-secs` 300 → **900** so 5 × 120s reads + backoff fit.
- Campaign path (`go-orchestrator`) keeps max-retries=5 and now also benefits from the per-type budget fix.

### Tests
- `tests/test-provider-retry-telemetry.rkt`: +2 (default=5; 5 timeout retries emitted via derived per-type budget; campaign=5).
- `tests/test-auto-retry.rkt`: +2 (default ceiling 900; ceiling aborts after 4 retries at 1000s > 900s).
- Updated `test-gsd-d8-provider-retry-scaling.rkt` + `test-partial-result-preservation.rkt` to the new 5-retry default (deliberate contract pins).
- Full fast suite: **1107 files / 16179 tests, 0 failed**.

### Verify
```
racket scripts/run-tests.rkt --suite fast
```

## v1.00.05 Wave 0 (#9392): Kimi thinking surfacing

### Problem
Kimi (Anthropic-compatible) returns `thinking` content blocks in its non-streaming response, but q dropped them:
- `anthropic-parse-response` only matched `text`/`tool_use`; `thinking` blocks fell through the raw catch-all.
- `eager-stream`'s `content->chunks` converted the raw block to an **empty text chunk** — thinking silently discarded.

- **`llm/anthropic/format.rkt`**: `anthropic-parse-response` translates `thinking` blocks into a thinking part (preserving `thinking` text + `signature`); `anthropic-parse-single-event` handles `thinking_delta` streaming chunks.
- **`llm/adapters/eager-stream.rkt`**: `content->chunks` emits `delta-thinking` for thinking parts (mirrors the OpenAI-compatible `reasoning_content` path).

title: fix(gsd): delivery verifier must match directory wave targets
body:
## Problem

v1.00.04 W5 failed delivery verification with `wave-failed (no wave target files changed: q/runtime/memory/policy.rkt, q/tests/memory/)` even though the wave delivered complete evidence (new test file `tests/memory/policy-boundary-test.rkt` + regenerated `tests/.coverage-manifest.json`, commit `70cec713`, PR #9389).

Root cause: the W5 wave doc declares a **directory target**:

```
- File: q/tests/memory/ (existing memory policy tests + new focused tests, e.g. ...)
```

`check-wave-files-changed` compared each wave target against the changed-file set **by exact path**. But `git diff --name-only` lists individual files, never directories — so the directory `q/tests/memory/` never matched the actual changed file `tests/memory/policy-boundary-test.rkt`. ## Fix

`wave-file-changed?` now treats a wave target whose original form ends in `/` as a **directory target** and matches it by **prefix**: any changed file under that directory satisfies the target. Exact-path matching is unchanged for concrete file targets.

title: fix(gsd): delivery verifier must accept committed branch delivery
body:
## Problem

The `/go` delivery verifier failed W0 of the v1.00.04 campaign with `wave-failed (delivery verification failed: files: no wave target files changed)` — even though the wave agent completed all Done-criteria and opened PR #9381 with the delivery commit `0429c2a1`.

## Root cause

`check-wave-files-changed` in `extensions/gsd/delivery-verifier.rkt` only detected **uncommitted** working-tree changes (`git diff --name-only HEAD`) plus untracked files. The test fixture (`make-git-file-change!`) never commits, so the verifier was designed for the "agent leaves work uncommitted" delivery style.

But wave docs may explicitly instruct the agent to **commit + push + open a PR** (v1.00.04 W0 does exactly that). After the agent commits, the working tree is clean, `git diff HEAD` is empty, and the verifier reports "no wave target files changed" — a **false negative** despite complete, GitHub-visible delivery evidence.

## Fix

`changed-files-set` now also includes commits on the current branch relative to its base (`origin/main` → `main`), using a three-dot diff (`base...HEAD`). Both delivery styles are now recognized:
- uncommitted working-tree changes (existing behavior, tests unchanged)
- committed feature-branch delivery (new)

## Verification

- New regression test: "approves committed delivery (wave committed + pushed + PR)" — commits the change on a feature branch with a clean working tree, asserts approval.
- All 12 tests in `tests/test-gsd-delivery-verifier.rkt` pass (11 original + 1 new).
- Verified against the **real failing case**: running `run-delivery-verification` on the actual repo (branch `v1.00.04-w0-impact-docs`, commit `0429c2a1`) now returns `approved? #t` with `files => changed: q/docs/TEST_CONVENTIONS.md`.

title: fix(gsd): progress-aware consecutive-tool breaker + higher ceilings (BUG-0016)
body:
## What & why

Fixes **BUG-0016** (`.planning/bugs/BUG-0016-wave-agent-consecutive-tool-breaker.md`): a `/go` wave agent doing a legitimate bulk metadata migration (1,264 files) was killed at 200 consecutive tool-only turns by the `current-max-consecutive-tool-calls` circuit breaker, leaving the last in-flight tool call with no result and marking the wave `failed`.

The root cause is not the tool executor — it is the runaway-loop safety guard misfiring on legitimate, progress-making bulk work. Three changes:

### (a) Progress-aware breaker (reset on distinct-file edits)
- `agent/iteration/loop-state.rkt`: new `edited-paths` field on `loop-counters` (tracks files edited in the current streak).
- `agent/iteration/counters.rkt`: `compute-next-counters` extracts edit/write target paths; a turn that edits a **NEW distinct file** resets `consecutive-tool-count` to 0 (implementation progress, not circling). Re-editing the same file keeps the streak so a same-file loop still fails closed.

### (b) Distinguish breaker-stops from dropped tool results in the wave outcome
- `runtime/iteration/step-executor.rkt`: `interpret-step` now stamps `toolLoopLimit` onto the final loop-result metadata when the breaker fired, so the wave runner reports **"tool loop limit reached"** instead of the ambiguous **"tool calls remain pending"**.

### (c) Higher ceilings
- `util/iteration/decision.rkt`: default `current-max-consecutive-tool-calls` **30 → 300**.
- `extensions/gsd/policy.rkt`: GSD campaign override `current-gsd-max-consecutive-tool-calls` **200 → 600** (`go-orchestrator.rkt:204` inherits the policy value).

## Tests
- `tests/test-iteration-counters-unit.rkt` +3: distinct-file edit resets; same-file re-edit keeps streak; multiple distinct edits reset once.
- `tests/test-iteration-counters.rkt` +2: same via helper-based suite.
- `tests/test-iteration-step-interpreter.rkt` +1: breaker-stop stamps `toolLoopLimit` onto final loop-result metadata (direct `interpret-step`).
- `tests/test-gsd-policy.rkt`: bounds updated for the new 600 ceiling.

Fixes the `/go` wave→coordinator→verification→next-wave stall. W0 of a new issue-less campaign (TDD/test-suite improvement) completed implementation + verification, but the coordinator marked it **wave-failed** because the delivery verifier falsely rejected on two grounds:

### 1. Issue-less campaigns rejected by branch check
`check-branch-matches` demanded `feature/issue-N-wave` derived from a STATE.md issue table. Campaigns that don't use per-wave GitHub issues run on `main`, so `branch=main expected=?` always failed.

**Fix:** the check now passes when no expected branch is derivable (issue-less campaign), and only honors STATE.md issue rows that reference the **current plan's wave doc** — stale rows left by a previous campaign (whose wave docs were replaced) are ignored instead of being misread as issue mappings.

### 2. Compile gate ran `raco make` on non-Racket files
`build-compile-gate` included every changed wave file — including `ci.yml` and `.md` docs — and `raco make` fails on non-module files, so the verify check always failed for waves touching CI/docs.

**Fix:** the compile gate now filters to Racket sources (`.rkt`/`.rktl`) only, and passes when no Racket targets changed (docs/CI-only wave) since the file-changed check already guarantees delivery evidence.

### Files
- `extensions/gsd/delivery-verifier.rkt` — branch check (issue-less + stale-row guard), compile-gate filter, verify-command fallback
- `tests/test-gsd-delivery-verifier.rkt` — +4 cases: issue-less main approval, stale STATE.md row ignored, non-Racket compile gate, plus fixture updates
- `README.md` — metrics re-sync

### Verification
- All 11 delivery-verifier tests pass; related GSD suites (go-orchestrator, wave-completion, wave-runner-port, campaign-state) pass
- `lint-all` 24 passed / 1 warning (non-blocking)
- Probe on the real new campaign: W0 and W5 now approve (previously both rejected)

Two latent issues surfaced by the user's live W3 re-test (2026-08-17 10:24+):

But even after deploying main, a **latent re-cap** would re-introduce 80: `tui-init.rkt` make-campaign-runner computed `(gsd-session-iteration-budget (dict-ref rt-config 'max-iterations 50))` — when rt-config lacks the key, budget caps at 50 → `resolve-max-iterations-hard` = max(50*8/5, 80) = **80**, silently defeating the v1.00.03 fix (budget 2000).

1. `tui/tui-init.rkt` — wave budget default now falls back to `(current-gsd-wave-max-iterations)` (2000) instead of 50, so the hard stop scales with the raised policy.
2. All GSD edit-limit sites → **2000**: `session-state.rkt` box default, `core.rkt` reset-all-gsd-state!, `command-handlers.rkt` launch-wave-executor + handle-plan-submit. Whole-form edits up to the tool's documented max now succeed.

title: fix: edit-tool leading-whitespace auto-fallback + D3 consecutive-tool ceiling 100→200 (#9366)
body:
Closes #9366.

## Why

Live W3 wave-failed (2026-08-17 09:52, session 01M07A6YCFN12E8E0FYJFHT9FT). The executor edited `tests/test-preferences-loader.rkt` with `old-text` whose leading whitespace was systematically **+1 space per level** (9/11/19 vs the file's actual 8/10/18). The edit tool does exact whitespace matching by default, so all 6 edit attempts failed `old-text not found`. The model kept recovering (read → grep → re-edit), never emitting a plain-text turn, and the D3 consecutive-tool breaker fired at **100** after ~19 min / 101 iterations → `tool-loop.limit-reached` → `wave-failed`.

## Fixes

1. **`edit-normalize.rkt`**: new `strip-leading?` normalization option + `leading-whitespace-normalization-options`; new `leading-ws-find-matches` that tolerates ONLY leading-whitespace (indentation) drift — threshold 1.0 means byte-exact content after stripping leading whitespace per line, no fuzzy similarity. Spans are expanded back over whitespace to the line start so replacement covers the file's real indentation.
2. **`edit-contract.rkt`**: `apply-edit-contract` auto-falls-back to the leading-ws match when exact fails — unique → apply, multiple → `ambiguous`, none → existing `not-found`/fuzzy path.
3. **`edit.rkt`**: success result now surfaces `Note: old-text matched after ignoring leading whitespace (indentation).` when the auto-fallback fired (fuzzy? true but fuzzy not requested).
4. **`policy.rkt`**: `current-gsd-max-consecutive-tool-calls` 100 → **200** — recovery loops that re-read/re-grep before retrying are not policy-killed while the runaway guard is retained.

## Tests

- `test-edit-normalize`: strip-leading normalization, coordinate mapping, ambiguity/content guards.
- `test-edit-matching-correctness`: auto-fallback applies when unique / `ambiguous` on repeats / `not-found` on content diff.
- `test-edit-execution-parity`: leading-ws mismatch now succeeds with the Note; genuine content mismatch still fails with full diagnostics (updated the old assertion that expected indentation mismatch to fail).
- `test-gsd-policy`: ceiling ≥ 200 and ≤ 400.

Verified: smoke (308 tests) + extensions (1511 tests) suites PASS; live probe of the exact incident now edits successfully.

**Problem (D8, campaign 81f9be4b W3 attempt-4):** 30/30 tool calls completed, then ONE transient 120 s SSE read timeout → progressive-stall circuit break → turn error → wave-failed, attempt consumed. The executor inherited the interactive provider-retry policy (max-retries 2, stall-breaker 2, 300 s ceiling) against a 1800 s wave budget.

**(A) Campaign-aware retry scaling:**
- `runtime/provider-retry.rkt`: `current-provider-retry-max-retries` / `stall-max-consecutive` / `ceiling-secs` parameters (defaults unchanged for interactive turns); `call-with-provider-retry` reads them.

**(B) Infra-meta-fix without attempt consumption:**
- `infra-failure?` classifier (go-orchestrator): classify-error domain network/provider, retry-exhausted marker, or stream/SSE/read-timeout messages → `'infra-failed` outcome in `prompt-run-result->outcome`.
- `wave-runner-port`: `'infra-failed` is now a valid terminal outcome kind.
- `run-campaign-wave`: infra-failed rolls back the `begin-attempt!` increment (status pending, attempt-count restored, current-attempt cleared), persists, and stops the campaign with a clear message so the user re-runs /go when the provider is healthy. Genuine agent/code failures still consume an attempt.

title: fix(gsd): /go campaign truth, quarantined gh-wave-finish, reasoning artifact integrity (v1.00.02, #9346)
body:
## Summary

Fixes all findings from the stopped `/go` campaign session analysis (issue #9346) and delivers them as a committed hotfix wave.

### /go execution truth & session budgets
- `/go` no longer marks a wave DONE on a normal model return: durable DONE now requires trusted delivery evidence (branch, commit, PR, issue closure); the advisory verifier can no longer emit authoritative approval events that contradict a fail-closed campaign result.
- `/go` refuses to start from a directory that cannot resolve Git (`git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree`); plan-validation errors are reported first.
- Campaign waves run on fresh isolated sessions; cancellation is wave-owned and can no longer shut down a global worker used by unrelated sessions.

### GitHub tool/root/staging safety
- `gh-wave-finish` is quarantined: validates the required `issue_number`/`files`/`commit_msg` contract (rejecting unknown properties and non-positive integers), then always fails before any repository, staging, or GitHub mutation.
- Staged-path inspection uses NUL-delimited `git diff --cached --name-only -z` output so whitespace/tab-bearing filenames cannot alias allowlisted paths.
- Extension inventory, GitHub README, and merge-path docs updated to describe the fail-before-mutation quarantine.

### TUI/GUI reasoning artifact integrity
- Terminal effects correlated with active canonical session/turn identity; stale/foreign-session completions can no longer clear unrelated active streams, status, or busy state.
- Token usage accounted once per canonical completion; empty/malformed identities never inflate or corrupt the cost tracker.
- Reasoning disclosure resolves canonical artifact IDs across Ctrl+O, `/toggle-detail`, and live render; live streaming reasoning renders under the same canonical ID.
- Reasoning persistence is UTF-8-byte bounded to 256 KiB at the scrollback boundary (including legacy rows); live reducer/transcript/GUI retention capped consistently with the 500-entry scrollback limit.
- GUI state mutation serialized under `gui-state-lock`; notification pending is invocation-local; transcript diffing treats changed artifact IDs as render changes.

## Verification
- Fast gate: **1096 files, 15,973/15,973 tests passing**.
- Changed-file focused suite: 34 files / 639 tests passing.

title: fix(release): release-readiness gate — registry/milestone-driven required-fix containment (W2, BUG-0008)
body:
Closes #9323

## What

Adds a release-readiness stage to the release preflight (extends W1, BUG-0007):

- `scripts/release-preflight.rkt --readiness <tag>` derives the required-fix list from
  a single source of truth — the bug registry (`.planning/bugs/INDEX.md` rows whose
  "Fixed in" targets this release) cross-checked against the `v<version>` GitHub
  milestone (via the milestone-gate helpers). No hand-maintained per-release list.
- Each required fix's landing SHA (recorded in the registry report's companion section
  when its PR merges) must satisfy `git merge-base --is-ancestor <fix-sha> <tagged-sha>`.
  Missing/non-ancestor → hard fail naming the BUG-ID/issue, the satisfying SHA, and the
  exact re-tag remediation.
- Wired into the existing fast `preflight` job in `.github/workflows/release.yml`
  (local git metadata + one tracker query) — a tag lacking a required fix is rejected
  before any expensive job starts.
- Documents the gate and the "record landing SHA on merge" convention in
  `docs/operations/release-runbook.md` and the registry README.

## Verification

- RED: tag predating a required fix → FAIL naming the missing BUG-ID (verified with
  `Q_BUG_REGISTRY` fixture: BUG-9999 → exit 1 with remediation).
- GREEN: tag containing all required fixes → readiness ok, exit 0.
- Derivation: gate output changes purely from registry content (no code changes).
